Ana (ML): Quick check — ran a SmoothQuant + activation-aware AWQ pipeline on the new 30B model for long-span contexts (30k / 80k / 120k). Seeing odd deltas on the summarization eval at 80k.
Chris (Infra): Can you paste the exact quant config and batch shape you used?
Ana (ML): Sure — config snippet: ```
quant: awq
activation_strategy: smoothquant
weight_bits: 8
use_fp8_kernels: false
kv_cache_shard: adaptive
batch_size: 1
max_seq: 120000
```
Jamal (Ops): Did you enable prefix caching? that changes effective token paths for long spans.
Ana (ML): I used prefix caching with eviction=LRU, window=64k. Also ran a run without caching to compare.
Sara (Evals): What was the metric delta? exact numbers help.
Ana (ML): ROUGE-L on longdoc summarization: baseline FP16 = 0.482, AWQ+SmoothQuant @30k = 0.475 (-0.007), @80k = 0.444 (-0.038), @120k = 0.447 (-0.035). So big drop at mid-long contexts only.
Mike (Runtime): Interesting — latency/cost profile OK? any KV cache eviction logs that match the drop times?
Ana (ML): Throughput/latency fine. Cost per token down ~2.8x. Eviction logs show frequent small evicts around 70–85k tokens when trunking the batch.
EvalBot: Regression alert created: ID Q-2003-42. Linked eval set: longdoc-summarize-1k-100k.
Sara (Evals): Could be activation shift due to SmoothQuant rescaling + AWQ per-block scale mismatch for large KV offsets. Do we have per-layer activation norms across sequences?
Ana (ML): I pulled layer act norms for layer 20, 40, 60. Norms drift significantly after ~60k tokens for layers 40+. I'll paste a tiny extract: ```layer40 mean_act: 0.98 -> 0.64 (after 70k)
layer60 mean_act: 1.02 -> 0.55 (after 75k)```
Chris (Infra): That aligns with kernel selection fallback: at long seqs runtime chooses different attention tiling which may interact with fused FP8 kernels vs INT8 paths. Did AWQ quantizer use per-channel zero-point or symmetric?
Ana (ML): AWQ used per-tensor scale with symmetric rounding. We tried per-channel too — similar trend but slightly less severe (~+0.004).
Mike (Runtime): Two hypothesis: 1) SmoothQuant scale computation uses a calibration batch that underestimates activation growth across long contexts. 2) KV cache shard/eviction causes partial re-normalization leading to inconsistent activation distributions.
Jamal (Ops): Repro steps to isolate: run deterministic seed, disable eviction, run with full fp16 (no quant) to see if caching alone causes drop.
Ana (ML): Ran fp16 w/ eviction disabled — no drop; metric stable ~0.482. So eviction interacting with quant path seems likely.
Sara (Evals): Can we try an AWQ variant with larger calibration context (simulate 120k) and SmoothQuant reweighting computed on long spans?
Ana (ML): I re-calibrated on 80k windows and re-ran AWQ+SmoothQuant: results improved to 0.462 at 80k (-0.02). Better but still gap.
Chris (Infra): Also try forced int8 kernels (disable fp8 kernels) to see if FP8 internal dynamic range is the issue.
Mike (Runtime): I'll spin a runtime test to force INT8 kernels for the attention/FF layers and keep AWQ scales. Should run in ~30m.
EvalBot: Scheduled job: runtime-test-2003007890-INT8-forced queued by Mike.
Ana (ML): Thanks. Also adding a small mitigation — fallback policy on deployment: if per-request summary score drops >0.02 compared to baseline, route traffic to fp16 for those callers. Can we get a perf SLA hit estimate?
Mike (Runtime): Fallback to fp16 increases cost ~3.5x for that request; but with sampling strategy it might be acceptable. We'll add per-route rollout with canary ratio.
Sara (Evals): Long-term we should add a calibration pass that includes simulated eviction + variable KV lifetimes when computing SmoothQuant scales. That might close the gap.
Jamal (Ops): Agree. Also file an infra ticket to make eviction traces easier to query per-request (right now we log but not indexed).
Ana (ML): Plan: 1) Mike run INT8-forced test and post logs. 2) I'll try AWQ calibration with eviction sim. 3) Sara re-run evals with new calibration. 4) If still gap, enable fp16 fallback policy canary.
Chris (Infra): Ping me if runtime test shows kernel fallbacks — want stack traces if we hit unexpected codepaths.
Mike (Runtime): Starting INT8 run now. ETA 28m.
Ana (ML): Thanks all. I'll update this thread with the calibration script and a short diff for SmoothQuant code changes when ready. :thumbsup:
